# App Store Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/app-store-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/app-store-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects app data from apps.apple.com and itunes.apple.com (Apple App Store), written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Code:** [`app_store.py`](app_store.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [App metadata](results/app_metadata.json) · [Reviews](results/reviews.json)

## What it scrapes

- App metadata (iTunes lookup API, with apps.apple.com fallback)
- App reviews (iTunes customer reviews RSS feed)

## Functions

- `scrape_app_metadata(app_id, country='us')` → `Dict`: scrape app metadata via the iTunes lookup API, falling back to the apps.apple.com page
- `scrape_reviews(app_id, country='us', max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape app reviews via the iTunes customer reviews RSS feed

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import app_store


async def main():
    app_metadata = await app_store.scrape_app_metadata("6448311069", "us")
    reviews = await app_store.scrape_reviews("6448311069", "us", max_pages=1)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/app_metadata.json`](results/app_metadata.json): `appId`, `bundleId`, `title`, `description`, `summary`, `developer`, `developerId`, `developerUrl`, `seller`, `sellerUrl`, `genre`, `genres`, `genreIds`, `price`, `free`, `currency`, `formattedPrice`, `score`, `scoreCurrentVersion`, `ratings`, `ratingsCurrentVersion`, `version`, `released`, `updated`, `contentRating`, `minimumOsVersion`, `fileSizeBytes`, `languages`, `icon`, `screenshots`, `ipadScreenshots`, `appletvScreenshots`, `supportedDevices`, `advisories`, `features`, `url`, `country`
- [`results/reviews.json`](results/reviews.json): `reviewId`, `userName`, `userUrl`, `title`, `content`, `score`, `version`, `voteSum`, `voteCount`, `updated`, `url`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`app_store.py`](app_store.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/app-store-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_app_scraping`, `test_reviews_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
